SourceEvidence.Short Source: Sase et al. 1997, Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 94(11):5646-5650
SourceEvidence.Notes:
Single-fluorophore polarization imaging shows sliding actin rotates once per ~1 um, far exceeding the 72-nm actin helical pitch - myosin 'runs' skipping protomers, with each kick primarily axial.

Relevance: Quantifies motor-driven filament axial rotation (~1 rev/um) as the field-free baseline vs any electro/magneto-orientation; demonstrates single-molecule orientation readout.

Four tropomyosins + Dia2 formin nucleate Tm4-decorated cortical filaments; myosin II is recruited Tm4-dependently and then anneals with Arp2/3-generated filaments to form contractile transverse arcs.

Relevance: Mechanistic transverse-arc assembly pathway (myosin recruitment) for the SF module; the actual mechanism paper behind the '2012 arc' seed.

Authoritative review: endogenous DC fields (~40-200 mV/mm) exist in all developing/regenerating tissues; lays out the physics and cellular mechanisms of field-directed cell behaviour.

Relevance: Canonical review framing physiological EF magnitudes (40-200 mV/mm) and mechanisms for the field-actuation program's baseline conditions.

F-actin behaves as a polyelectrolyte: multivalent cations above a valence-dependent threshold bundle filaments (ionic-strength dependent), analogous to DNA condensation - a generic charge-driven mechanism.

Relevance: Establishes the polyelectrolyte / fixed-charge nature of actin that any E-field-on-filament actuation model requires.

Kinetic model with FH2 gating (open/closed) + FH1 multi-site profilin-actin transfer predicts an optimal profilin concentration maximizing elongation, with high profilin suppressing growth.

Relevance: Closed-form formin-elongation model usable as an acceptance oracle for the FF formin kinetics.

SourceEvidence.Short Source: Haraguchi et al. 2022, Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 119(8):e2120962119
SourceEvidence.Notes:
Four Chara myosin XI cloned; XI-1/XI-2 motor domains 3.2x/2.8x faster than prior CcXI; a chimeric XI-1 reaches 60 um/s (~10x fast skeletal-muscle myosin), explaining ~70 um/s streaming; 2.8-A crystal structure implicates actin-binding loops.

Relevance: Upper-bound motor velocity (60-70 um/s) setting the streaming forcing amplitude. Corrects the seed's mis-attributed 'Kashiyama 2021' to this verified PNAS DOI (Kashiyama is not an author; this is the published form of bioRxiv 2021.05.06.442907).

Comprehensive transient-aqueous-pore theory of electroporation: transmembrane potential ~0.5-1 V drives pore formation and sets reversible vs irreversible thresholds and pore energetics.

Relevance: Reference theory for the field-strength threshold (~0.5-1 V TMP) above which membrane shielding fails and the field couples into the cytoplasm.

Functionalized magnetic nanoparticles inside living cells act as displaceable nanoscopic hot spots that, under magnetic force, locally trigger Rac-GTPase signalling and remodel the actin cytoskeleton / cell morphology.

Relevance: The intracellular SPION actuation paper - direct in-cytoplasm magnetic force application with downstream cytoskeletal response, the core of the field-actuation concept.

SourceEvidence.Short Source: Gardel et al. 2008, J Cell Biol 183(6):999-1005
SourceEvidence.Notes:
Traction stress vs F-actin retrograde-flow speed is biphasic with a threshold flow speed of ~8-10 nm/s independent of FA density/age: inverse (traction rises as flow slows) near the edge, direct in mature FAs.

Relevance: Primary quantitative acceptance target (biphasic traction-flow law, 8-10 nm/s threshold) for the FF molecular-clutch/traction actuation module.

Chimeric high-/low-speed myosin XI-2 (swapping Chara vs human motor domains) accelerated/decelerated streaming and correspondingly enlarged/shrank the plant - a causal link between streaming velocity and organ size.

Relevance: Direct myosin-XI actuation-of-streaming experiment tying motor speed to advective-transport output (the seed 'Tominaga myosin XI' paper).

Experimentally validates the Schwan equation for AC-field-induced transmembrane potential; measured critical breakdown potentials 0.33-0.53 V and inferred cytoplasm resistivity 910-1100 Ohm-cm.

Relevance: Quantitative induced-TMP and cytoplasm-conductivity values (breakdown 0.33-0.53 V; 910-1100 Ohm-cm) for an E-field-shielding/electroporation actuation model.

Electrostatic (polycation) vs steric (PEG) bundling of F-actin, DNA, microtubules and vimentin have opposite dependence on ionic strength and filament concentration - the shared polyelectrolyte nature dictates behaviour.

Relevance: Generalizes the actin polyelectrolyte result across all cytoskeletal filaments; supports a unified charge-based field-response treatment.

Local cortex relaxation does not stop blebbing on the far side, so hydrostatic pressure does NOT equilibrate over ~10 um / ~10 s; the cytoplasm is a poroelastic contractile network infiltrated by cytosol.

Relevance: Foundational poroelastic-cytoplasm evidence (non-equilibration ~10 um/10 s) underpinning the Biot/FSI two-way coupling and spatial pressure-field work in the FF engine.

SourceEvidence.Short Source: Thievessen et al. 2013, J Cell Biol 202(1):163-177
SourceEvidence.Notes:
Vinculin acts as the molecular clutch: its actin interaction slows F-actin flow in maturing FAs and generates high ECM traction, yet FA growth rate tracks flow speed independently of vinculin.

Relevance: Identifies the specific clutch protein (vinculin) coupling flow->traction; informs which linker the FF clutch bond should represent.

Actomyosin pulls the nucleus forward via nesprin-3, physically partitioning cytoplasm into fore/aft compartments and pressurizing the front to drive lamellipodia-independent lobopodial 3D migration; nesprin-3 knockdown equalizes intracellular pressure.

Relevance: Nucleus-as-piston compartmentalized-pressure mechanism - a nucleus<->cortex load path and pressure-compartmentalization the internal-coupling/CFD model must represent.

SourceEvidence.Short Source: Oakes et al. 2012, J Cell Biol 196(3):363-374
SourceEvidence.Notes:
A stress-fiber template (formin/alpha-actinin-1 dependent) is required for FA compositional maturation; maturation still occurs when cellular tension is reduced ~80% -> tension is necessary but not sufficient.

Relevance: Constrains FA-maturation logic (structural SF template vs pure tension; ~80% tension-reduction datum) for adhesion/SF coupling.

Piconewton tensile force on the filament accelerates formin (mDia1/mDia2) dissociation by orders of magnitude, overriding profilin stabilization, via two distinct force-selected dissociation pathways.

Relevance: Force-dependent formin detachment -> the mechanistic, force-coupled formin kinetics for the field-actuation program.

Foundational treatment of tissue/cell-suspension dielectrics and the alpha/beta/gamma dispersions - the basis for membrane-capacitance shielding and the Schwan equation for field-induced transmembrane potential.

Relevance: Origin of the membrane dielectric / beta-dispersion model governing how much of an applied external field is shielded vs reaches the cytoplasm. (Book-series chapter; typed as review.)

SourceEvidence.Short Source: Gartzke & Lange 2002, Am J Physiol Cell Physiol 283(5):C1333-C1346
SourceEvidence.Notes:
Proposes the polyelectrolyte microvillar F-actin bundle as the cellular interaction site for weak EM/magnetic fields via nonlinear cable-like cation conduction through condensed ion clouds (stochastic-resonance / Brownian-motor framing).

Relevance: Bridges field-on-filament and magnetic-actuation topics - a mechanistic hypothesis for how weak external fields could couple to charged actin.

SourceEvidence.Short Source: Footer et al. 2007, Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 104(7):2181-2186
SourceEvidence.Notes:
Optical-trap growth of ~8 parallel filaments stalls at ~1 pN (single-filament stall load), with large length fluctuations indicating only the longest filament touches the barrier -> dynamic instability limits bundle force.

Relevance: Direct experimental stall-force calibration (~1 pN) for polymerization actuation in bundle geometry.

Diffusion-drift-reaction modeling in 3D cell geometry: rear-disassembly/front-assembly + diffusion set up a G-actin gradient transporting monomer forward; convective cytoplasmic flow contributes little; relaxation time ~10-100 s.

Relevance: Quantitative diffusion-vs-advection G-actin transport model (relaxation ~10-100 s) underpinning the transport-limited-actin analysis.

SourceEvidence.Short Source: Kovar & Pollard 2004, Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 101(41):14725-14730
SourceEvidence.Notes:
Filament growth between an immobilized formin and an anchor buckles segments as short as 0.7 um, demonstrating single-filament polymerization forces >1 pN (near theoretical max) via insertional assembly.

Relevance: Direct single-filament polymerization-force datum (>1 pN) for the actin-polymerization actuation (protrusion) force scale.

Review of galvanotactic mechanisms (Ca2+ push-pull, voltage-gated Na+ channels, surface charge, protein electrophoresis); strongly metastatic prostate/breast cells are more galvanotactic and can migrate oppositely to weakly metastatic cells.

Relevance: Cancer-cell electrotaxis mechanisms and the Nav-channel angle relevant to MCF7/MDA field-response modeling.

SourceEvidence.Short Source: Tojkander, Gateva & Lappalainen 2012, J Cell Sci 125(8):1855-1864
SourceEvidence.Notes:
Review consolidating stress-fiber subtypes (dorsal SF, transverse arc, ventral SF), their assembly, turnover, and contractile/mechanosensing roles.

Relevance: The J Cell Sci 2012 SF review named in the seed; reference map for SF-subtype definitions and dynamics.

SourceEvidence.Short Source: Fabry et al. 2001, Phys Rev Lett 87(14):148102
SourceEvidence.Notes:
Magnetic-bead microrheology collapses onto a single weak-power-law master curve g*(f) ~ f^x (soft glassy rheology), unifying cell mechanical response across drugs and conditions.

Relevance: Scaling / soft-glass framework for interpreting bead-actuation microrheology against the FF/DCM viscoelastic response.

Formin elongation rate rises with the number of FH1 polyproline/profilin tracks; FH1 binding of profilin-actin is rate-limiting for subunit delivery up to rates >=88 subunits/s; profilin inhibits FH2 nucleation.

Relevance: Quantitative FH1-profilin delivery model (>=88 s^-1) for formin processive-elongation parameters.

SourceEvidence.Short Source: Stracke et al. 2002, Biochem Biophys Res Commun 293(1):602-609
SourceEvidence.Notes:
Single microtubules migrate toward the anode with electrophoretic mobility ~2.6e-4 cm^2/Vs (~0.19 net electron charge per tubulin dimer, IEP ~pH 4.2); DC fields also reorient kinesin-gliding MTs.

Relevance: Quantitative MT charge/mobility (2.6e-4 cm^2/Vs) for modeling electric-field actuation and orientation of the microtubule compartment.

Actomyosin sliding force carries a right-handed torque: a fixed-front actin filament forms a left-handed superhelix before supercoiling, revealing axial rotation of the filament during sliding.

Relevance: Control paper - filament rotation from motor torque (not external field), needed to disambiguate field-induced vs motor-induced filament reorientation.

Review: myosin-XI-driven organelle movement entrains cytosol to drive cyclosis; streaming velocity varies with cell type, developmental stage and species and shapes intracellular molecular gradients.

Relevance: Biological grounding for the streaming/advective-transport module - connects motor mechanics to emergent cytosol flow and gradients.

SourceEvidence.Short Source: Goldstein, Tuval & van de Meent 2008, Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 105(10):3663-3667
SourceEvidence.Notes:
First quantitative advection-diffusion theory of rotational cytoplasmic streaming (Chara/Nitella); scalar-mixing enhancement depends strongly on helical flow pitch and peaks at Nitella's exponential growth phase.

Relevance: Canonical model coupling motor-driven fluid entrainment to intracellular scalar transport - the physics the CFD/advective-transport channel must reproduce.

Review: SF subtypes (dorsal, transverse arc, ventral) differ in molecular composition and spatially/temporally partition myosin-II contractility during mesenchymal migration.

Relevance: Subtype-composition reference for parameterizing distinct SF populations in the model.

Magnetic twisting cytometry through integrin-bound beads: cytoskeletal stiffness rises in direct proportion to applied stress and requires intact microtubules + intermediate filaments + microfilaments (tensegrity).

Relevance: Founding magnetic-bead actuation + tensegrity result - directly supports the MT-compression/actin-tension tensegrity work in the codebase.

SourceEvidence.Short Source: van de Meent, Tuval & Goldstein 2008, Phys Rev Lett 101(17):178102
SourceEvidence.Notes:
Chiral helical wall forcing produces transverse Dean-like vortices; strongly enhanced lateral transport and longitudinal homogenization emerge above a critical transverse Peclet number (boundary-layer scaling).

Relevance: Advective-mixing theory: a chiral flow field boosts transport - informs modeling streaming as an actuated CFD transporter.

Barbed-end elongation is diffusion-limited (k+ ~ 1e7 M^-1 s^-1 per centipoise, extrapolating through the origin vs viscosity); inert macromolecular crowders raise k+ via an excluded-volume activity increase.

Relevance: Justifies diffusion/viscosity dependence of elongation and crowding acceleration; ties polymerization to the cytoplasm-rheology/transport program.

Keratocyte galvanotaxis is insensitive to membrane potential/ion fluxes but fails below pH 6 and slows with aqueous viscosity -> lateral electrophoresis of charged membrane components, not ion transport, is the primary directional sensing mechanism.

Relevance: Mechanistic basis for E-field actuation acting via surface-charge electrophoresis rather than currents - relevant to modeling field effects on the membrane.

Physiological-strength DC electric fields are the dominant directional cue in wound healing; genetic loss of PI(3)Kgamma abolishes electrotaxis while PTEN deletion enhances it, placing electrotaxis on the chemotaxis PI3K/PTEN axis.

Relevance: Foundational E-field-actuation-of-migration paper anchoring the electrotaxis signalling axis that field-actuation experiments perturb.

Peripheral MLCK-dependent SFs show lower effective elasticity and higher plateau retraction than central ROCK-dependent SFs; SF populations share load and can absorb one another's roles.

Relevance: Regional SF mechanical heterogeneity + load-sharing for spatially resolved SF modeling.

Laser-severed single stress fibers recoil as actomyosin-tensed viscoelastic cables (prestress); recoil is abolished by MLCK inhibition; the ECM deforms as a physical extension of the cytoskeleton.

Relevance: Quantitative viscoelastic-prestress single-SF datum; acceptance oracle for single-SF mechanics in the stress-fiber target build.

FH1-FH2 formin is a processive barbed-end motor that requires profilin; it increases the profilin-actin association rate constant ~15-fold and couples ATP hydrolysis to processive polymerization.

Relevance: Mechanistic basis for formin-accelerated elongation (~15x) in the FF formin/protrusion kinetics.

Review comparing electrotaxis across cell types; implicates electro-migration of surface receptors/ion channels and highlights EFs as a precisely controllable guidance cue relative to chemical gradients.

Relevance: Comparative synthesis for choosing field-actuation protocols; complements the mechanism papers.

Scallop theorem: at Re<<1 (bacteria ~1e-4-1e-5) reciprocal motion yields zero net displacement; inertia is irrelevant and only a non-reciprocal shape-sequence propels.

Relevance: Sets the inertialess Stokes regime governing all intracellular cytosol/organelle transport and the no-inertia force-balance underlying the FF/DCM solvers.

SourceEvidence.Short Source: Vallotton et al. 2004, Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 101(26):9660-9665
SourceEvidence.Notes:
qFSM maps coupled F-actin flow + net assembly/disassembly; ~90% of lamellipodial polymer disassembles at the lamellipodium-lamellum junction, with contraction-coupled depolymerization in the convergence zone.

Relevance: Quantitative flow+turnover field (~90% junction disassembly) the transport-limited-actin and retrograde-flow modules are validated against.

Founding conceptual framework for growth-cone advance: actin assembles at the leading membrane edge and undergoes rearward (retrograde) flow / treadmilling, with membrane-cytoskeleton coupling converting flow into traction. Qualitative (no number).

Relevance: Conceptual root of the retrograde-flow + molecular-clutch paradigm that the FF molecular-clutch/traction module implements.

Wounds instantly generate injury currents producing lateral fields of 40-200 mV/mm; removing the field slows healing ~25%, and clinical EF stimulation increases healing rate 13-50%.

Relevance: Quantitative endogenous-field magnitudes (40-200 mV/mm) and causal wound-field evidence underpinning the electrotaxis program.

FRAP + constrained modeling of steady treadmilling protrusions shows molecular diffusion alone cannot resupply G-actin to the leading edge; a vectorial anterograde transport (velocity <1 um/s, diffusivity ~2 um^2/s) is required.

Relevance: Core evidence that leading-edge actin assembly is transport/advection-limited (CFD-transport program); the 2023 BiophysJ analysis.

Magnetic-bead microrheometer (forces up to ~1e4 pN on 4.5 um beads) yields a local surface shear modulus ~2-4e-3 Pa*m and apparent cytoplasmic viscosity ~2e3 Pa*s, with a ~7 um screened elastic-field cutoff.

Relevance: Bead-force ranges + local viscoelastic/cytoplasm-viscosity numbers to calibrate magnetic actuation and cytoplasm drag/FSI. Caveat: apparent ~2e3 Pa*s (bead microrheometry) is method-dependent and >> the ~65 Pa*s MCF7 rotational-spectroscopy value (Dessard2024).

SourceEvidence.Short Source: Burnette et al. 2011, Nat Cell Biol 13(4):371-381
SourceEvidence.Notes:
Lamellipodial actin is condensed by myosin II into an actin arc that moves rearward and slows at FAs; the arc mechanically bridges lamellipodium and lamella to advance the leading edge.

Relevance: Links protrusion actin -> arc -> adhesion; structurally couples the retrograde-flow and stress-fiber modules.

Review: the molecular clutch is a conserved 3D nano-architecture of mechanosensitive protein-protein interactions (integrin-talin-vinculin-actin) transmitting cytoskeletal force to the ECM.

Relevance: Authoritative clutch-architecture review framing the multi-protein force-transmission stack the FF adhesion module abstracts.

Two molecularly distinct G-actin pools feed lamellipodia: a cytosolic thymosin-beta4-bound monomer pool targeted to formins/leading edge (elevated G/F ratio for protrusion) and a locally recycled lamellipodial F-actin pool.

Relevance: Establishes non-homogeneous monomer pools + spatial targeting constraining the transport-limited actin-resupply model. Caveat: seed mis-placed it in PNAS; it is Cell Reports.

SourceEvidence.Short Source: Colombelli et al. 2009, J Cell Sci 122(10):1665-1679
SourceEvidence.Notes:
SF laser nanosurgery + a computational SF force model: zyxin relocalizes to high-tension intermediate anchor points and measured localization matches the computed force distribution -> direct force sensing along stress fibers.

Relevance: Force-along-SF computational model + mechanosensing datum; template for the FF SF force-distribution readout.

Fluorescent speckle microscopy resolves two colocalized F-actin networks: a lamellipodium whose polymer disassembles within ~1-3 um of the edge, and a lamella where actomyosin contraction couples to adhesions.

Relevance: Defines the two-zone (lamellipodium vs lamella) retrograde-flow kinematics the FF cortex/protrusion transport model must reproduce.

Feedback optical-trap measurement of a single myosin-actin interaction: ~11 nm working steps at low load and 3-4 pN single-molecule isometric force transients.

Relevance: Single-motor step-size (~11 nm) and force (3-4 pN) calibration for the mechanistic myosin-II head model.

DecisionLedger.Decision Text: Split the Notion KB into 8 atomic relational DBs (SourceEvidence/KnowledgeClaim/ModelContract/Parameter/ValidationGate/CodeMapping/RunResult/DecisionLedger) by data type. Seed critical path first; legacy Unit pages kept as canonical prose.
DecisionLedger.Rationale: Legacy KB mixed 5 truth types under one KU number; 'KU-3.5 failed' conflated literature claim with implementation gate. Atomization fixes retrieval granularity + the claim/contract/gate distinction.

DecisionLedger.Decision Text: Resolve H.5-lamellipodium vs KB-Unit-5-collective KU-5.x collision by Option A: add an H.5 retrieval entry pointing to KB Unit 3 + collision warning; no renumber. Forward primary keys KB-5.x (collective) vs H5-LP-x (lamellipodium); legacy KU-5.x kept as alias.
DecisionLedger.Rationale: KU IDs are shared scientific contracts (briefs/configs/tests). Renumber is gate-contract-level; pure addition is safe and reversible. Splits the colliding KU-5.1 into two distinct claims -- KB-5.1 (collective jamming) and H5-LP-1 (lamellipodium density) -- kept as aliases.

DecisionLedger.Decision Text: Diagnostic (isolated worktree diag/gamma-r0eff, opt-in flag diag_r0_eff_delivery, NOT merged): wired the documented r0_eff=max(r-s_grip,0) so grip_walk's s_grip accumulator delivers force F=k*min(r,s_grip). On gripwalk_tier1 (repo params) it delivered a PHYSICAL sub-stall force (F/F_stall mean 0.196, max 0.614 <=1) yet gamma_total floored at 4.0e-5 mN/m - indistinguishable from grip_walk-OFF (4.9e-5) and binned_r0 (3.2e-5). Conclusion: the s_grip 'dead-for-force' delivery gap (docstring myosin.py:184-188 vs impl myosin.py:1385 'CH1 NO requantization') is REAL but is NOT the KU-3.5 active-tension floor cause. Proposes redirecting the active-gamma effort to recruitment + force-aggregation, NOT per-head generation.
DecisionLedger.Rationale: Confirms+sharpens the authoritative 'force-aggregation' wall (commit 97f6b3e). Signature: g_soft rose ~3x but g_rigid (~85% of gamma_total) unchanged; fewest engaged heads (30 vs binned_r0 73). Per-head force IS generated and delivered sub-stall but does not aggregate into the shell-tension channel the gate measures. F/F_stall<=1 guardrail satisfied -> null is not a clamp artifact. Open lever: recruitment (engaged-head count) + transmission/coherence into the rigid channel. Worktree preserved at /Users/sw1/ffn_gammadiag for Lead inspection; not merged.
DecisionLedger.Decision: gamma-floor: s_grip->r0_eff delivery (P1) refuted as the active-tension cause
